## 오늘의 한국 경제 흐름 요약

중동 전쟁 장기화로 인한 고유가 기조가 국내 경제 전반에 파급 영향을 미치고 있는 가운데, 건설공사비가 7개월 연속 최고치를 경신하며 부동산 시장의 비용 부담을 가중시키고 있다. 이러한 공사비 상승 압력 속에서도 서울 아파트 매매·전세 상승률은 소폭 둔화되었고, 특히 강남·용산 등 고가 지역에서는 매매가 하락세가 이어지며 시장이 조정 국면에 접어드는 모습이다. 한편 소비 시장은 상대적으로 견조한 흐름을 보여, 올 1분기 카드 승인액이 322조 원을 넘어 전년 대비 7.2% 증가하였는데, 온라인 쇼핑 확대와 여행 선예약 수요 증가가 주된 동력으로 작용했다. 종합하면, 대외 에너지 리스크와 건설 비용 상승이 공급 측면의 불확실성을 높이는 반면, 민간 소비는 회복세를 유지하는 **엇갈린 경제 흐름**이 오늘의 주된 특징이라 할 수 있다.

key_headlines.summary: Seoul apartment sales and jeonse (lease) price increases have slowed marginally, with Gangnam and Yongsan districts still experiencing price declines amid stricter loan regulations.

key_headlines.title: Construction Costs Hit 7-Month High; Middle East War Accelerates Price Increases
key_headlines.summary: Construction costs have reached record levels for seven consecutive months, with the ongoing Middle East conflict expanding inflationary pressures in the sector.

key_headlines.title: Q1 Card Approval Transactions Surge 7.2% to 322.1 Trillion Won
key_headlines.summary: First quarter card approval transactions reached 322.1 trillion won, up 7.2%, driven by increased online shopping and advance travel bookings.

key_headlines.title: High Oil Prices Expected to Persist Beyond Conflict Resolution
key_headlines.summary: Market analysts project that elevated crude oil prices will remain elevated even after Middle East tensions resolve, driven by strategic oil reserve buildup by major economies.

key_headlines.title: Korea's F4 Economic Leadership Meets for First Time Under New Central Bank Governor
key_headlines.summary: Vice Premier convenes expanded macroeconomic and financial meeting with new Bank of Korea Governor and financial regulators, establishing 24-hour market monitoring amid currency and oil price volatility concerns.

sections.Hot Economy News: Seoul's real estate market shows cooling momentum with apartment sales and jeonse price increases slowing modestly, while Gangnam and Yongsan districts continue declining. Construction costs have hit record highs for seven consecutive months, accelerated by Middle East geopolitical tensions. Q1 card approval transactions surged 7.2% to 322.1 trillion won, driven by online shopping and advance travel bookings. Oil prices remain elevated due to expectations of strategic reserve expansion beyond the conflict period. Korea's top economic officials convened for their first meeting under the new Bank of Korea governor to establish coordinated response mechanisms for currency and oil price volatility.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: The European Central Bank held interest rates steady amid inflation concerns stemming from Middle East conflicts, maintaining deposit rates at 2.00%, base rate at 2.15%, and marginal lending rate at 2.40%. The Bank of England similarly paused rate adjustments at 3.75%, prioritizing monitoring of energy price shocks and inflation risks. Both central banks acknowledged increased upside risks to inflation and downside risks to economic growth. Korean securities firms project the Bank of Korea may implement two rate hikes of 0.25 percentage points each this year, reversing the extended pause stance. Concerns about potential stagflation similar to the 1970s oil crises have emerged, though modern monetary and fiscal systems are considered more robust.
sections.Financial Markets: The Korean stock market declined 1.38% to close at 6598.87, falling below the 6,600 level amid international crude oil surges and dovish interest rate holds. The KOSDAQ also fell as foreign investors net sold 1.46 trillion won in equities. Entertainment and culture sectors led declines at 2.30%, while real estate dropped 1.44%. The U.S. Federal Reserve held rates steady at 3.50%, but with unusual dissent from three FOMC members opposing dovish guidance language, reflecting the deepest policy divisions since 1992. NYSE markets showed mixed performance amid oil price volatility and monetary policy uncertainty.
sections.Industry & Technology: LG Energy Solution secured a major 10 trillion won battery supply contract with German automaker BMW for electric vehicle cylindrical batteries totaling 100GWh, signaling recovery for Korea's secondary battery sector. Samsung SDI also recently began EV battery supplies to Mercedes-Benz, offering industry optimism. The 12th basic electricity supply plan signals potential additions of new nuclear power plants beyond the single large reactor and SMR approved in the 11th plan, as renewables alone prove insufficient for carbon neutrality goals. Semiconductor exports surpassed 30 billion dollars for two consecutive months with total April exports reaching 85.8 billion dollars.
sections.Real Estate: Seoul apartment monthly rental transactions crossed the 50% threshold for the first time, reaching 50.8% in Q1 2026, accelerating the 'jeonse-to-monthly-rent conversion' trend due to stricter lending regulations and jeonse supply shortages. Entire Seoul housing monthly rental share reached 70.5% in Q1. The smaller 59-square-meter unit supply is now exceeding the standard 84-square-meter units in new apartments due to lower construction costs and higher developer profits. Gangnam districts are experiencing selective price rebounds ahead of capital gains tax surcharges on multi-property owners effective May 10, with properties under 1.5 billion won seeing increased demand.
sections.International Economy: Fed Chairman Jerome Powell declared his intention to remain as a Federal Reserve Board member after his term ends, amid political pressure from the Trump administration regarding central bank independence and facility relocations. The FOMC showed unprecedented division with four dissenting votes on rate policy guidance, the largest dissent since 1992, with some members opposing dovish language. Powell criticized the Trump administration for endangering Federal Reserve independence during his final press conference as chairman. Brent crude oil surged to 126.41 dollars per barrel, the highest level since June 2022, driven by escalating U.S.-Iran military tensions and ceasefire negotiations deadlock.
sections.AI & Economy: Major U.S. tech giants Meta, Microsoft, Alphabet, and Amazon posted earnings surprises in Q1, with cloud services driving growth—Microsoft Azure revenues surged 40% while overall sales reached 123 trillion won. Cumulative AI infrastructure investment across these four companies exceeded 100 trillion won, with profits demonstrating AI monetization success. Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix achieved unprecedented 95 trillion won combined Q1 operating profits, prompting expert recommendations for bold M&A acquisitions in AI companies like Anthropic. CPU-based AI PC demand is rising alongside AI agent growth, shifting market focus from GPU and memory semiconductors to processor chips, as evidenced by Intel's performance gains.
sections.Others: Public institutions' debt ratio declined 6.4 percentage points to 174.1% in 2025, with new hiring expanding by approximately 7,000 positions to 27,000 employees at an average annual salary of 74 million won. Government announced a complete overhaul of foreign worker policies through integrated lifecycle management, including eased workplace mobility restrictions and extended employment periods through revised employment permit systems. Domestic AI semiconductor startups including Rebellion, PuriosaAI, and DeepX are preparing IPOs through robust pre-IPO fundraising activities. Wuri Bank hosted a U.S. investment briefing for Korean SMEs and ventures amid rising U.S. tariff negotiations and protectionism.
